Revelation began with true dreams and the angel in Hira commanding the Prophet to recite; Khadija reassured him, Waraqa recognised it, and after a pause came 'You who are shrouded'.
The Prophet moved his tongue to memorise revelation as Gabriel brought it, until Allah told him not to hasten, for He would collect it; then he listened and afterwards recited.
Told by a verse not to move his tongue in haste, the Prophet listened attentively while Gabriel recited and, when Gabriel left, recited as he had.
Al-Bara said the last verse revealed was the one on kalala and the last complete sura revealed was Sura Bara'at.
When Gabriel delayed and the Prophet, ill, did not rise for night prayer, polytheists said he was forsaken, and Allah revealed that his Lord had not forsaken him.
Revelation came to the Prophet like a ringing bell or through an angel in human form, weighing on him, changing his colour, bowing his head and making his forehead sweat.
Allah sent revelation to the Prophet in quick succession before his death, and on the day he died it came most abundantly.
